bearing.guide.fan_direction.header: Encased Fans: Which Way the Air Goes
bearing.guide.fan_direction.text_1: Spin an Encased Fan and it pushes a stream of air out of its front
bearing.guide.fan_direction.text_2: Reverse the rotation and the fan pulls air in instead; faster rotation makes the stream reach further
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_1: An air stream that flows through lava comes out hot
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_2: Heated air turns the items it touches into their smelting results
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_3: Raw food would simply burn up in there
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_4: Blow the air through fire instead to smoke food
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_5: Blow the air through water instead and the stream will wash items
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_6: Washing opens up a few new kinds of processing
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_7: A faster fan only reaches further: the items are not processed any quicker
bearing.guide.fan_processing.text_8: Items resting on Depots or moving along Belts can be processed by the stream as well
bearing.guide.millstone.text_1: A Millstone grinds the items put into it
bearing.guide.millstone.text_2: Cogwheels next to it can drive it from the side
bearing.guide.millstone.text_3: Drop or insert the items in from above
bearing.guide.millstone.text_4: Once it has finished, [Right-Click] it to take out the result
bearing.guide.millstone.text_5: Funnels and other machines can pull the output out automatically
bearing.guide.crushing_wheels.text_1: Two Crushing Wheels side by side make a powerful grinder
bearing.guide.crushing_wheels.text_2: Power them so that their facing sides both turn inward, toward each other
bearing.guide.crushing_wheels.text_3: Anything dropped or inserted between them from above gets crushed
bearing.guide.crushing_wheels.text_4: Machines like Chutes and Depots can feed them and collect the products
bearing.guide.mechanical_mixer.text_1: A Mechanical Mixer above a Basin can automate a number of crafting recipes
bearing.guide.mechanical_mixer.text_2: It handles every shapeless crafting recipe, and some extra mixing recipes too
bearing.guide.mechanical_mixer.text_3: Certain recipes only work when a Blaze Burner heats the Basin
bearing.guide.mechanical_mixer.text_4: If two recipes overlap, set the filter slot to pick the one you want
bearing.guide.mechanical_press.text_1: Whatever is set down beneath the Mechanical Press gets pressed
bearing.guide.mechanical_press.text_2: Throw the input onto a Depot under the Press, or put it there by hand
bearing.guide.mechanical_press.text_3: Items can also arrive on a Mechanical Belt...
bearing.guide.mechanical_press.text_4: ...where the Press stops them, presses them and lets them move on
bearing.guide.mechanical_press_compactin: When the Press works on a Basin, it compacts the items inside
This covers every fully filled 2x2 or 3x3 crafting recipe, along with a few special ones
Some of them need a Blaze Burner heating the Basin
When two recipes clash, choose one using the filter slot
bearing.guide.basin.text_1: Machines draw their ingredients, items and fluids alike, from a Basin
bearing.guide.basin.text_2: Whatever a process produces, the Basin tries to hand down to a block beside and below it
bearing.guide.basin.text_3: With a fitting block there, the Basin grows a little output spout on that side
bearing.guide.basin.text_4: Chests, Depots, Belts and other inventories all work there
bearing.guide.basin.text_5: Products then drop into the inventory underneath
bearing.guide.basin.text_6: With no output spout, the Basin keeps whatever it makes
bearing.guide.basin.text_7: That is handy when a product is an ingredient for the next step
bearing.guide.basin.text_8: The products you want must then be pulled out of the Basin
bearing.guide.basin.text_9: Give the extractor a filter so it leaves unprocessed ingredients alone
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_1: A Blaze can be caught: [Right-Click] it holding an Empty Blaze Burner
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_2: A Blaze spawner works too: use the burner on it directly
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_3: Now you hold a perfect source of heat for many machines
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_4: Just want the look? Flint and Steel lights an Empty Blaze Burner too
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_5: Use an item touched by souls on it to change the colour of the flame
bearing.guide.empty_blaze_burner.text_6: Without a Blaze inside, though, they cannot heat any machine
bearing.guide.blaze_burner.text_1: Set under a Basin, a Blaze Burner supplies the heat some recipes call for
bearing.guide.blaze_burner.text_2: To do so, the Blaze needs to be fed something that burns
bearing.guide.blaze_burner.text_3: Feeding it a Blaze Cake makes it burn hotter still
bearing.guide.blaze_burner.text_4: Deployers or Mechanical Arms can take care of the feeding for you
bearing.guide.depot.text_1: A Depot acts like a single belt segment that does not move
bearing.guide.depot.text_2: Items go on and come off again with a [Right-Click]
bearing.guide.depot.text_3: Machines can process what sits on it, just like on a belt
bearing.guide.depot.text_4: ...and Mechanical Arms can pick items up from it
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_1: Hold an Ejector, Sneak and [Right-Click] a block to choose where it will throw
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_2: Once placed, it throws things toward the chosen spot
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_3: The target may be higher, lower or further away, as long as it is in range
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_4: It must lie straight ahead of the Ejector, never off to one side
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_5: If you never pick a target, it just lobs items one block forward
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_6: Rotational force winds it up and readies it to launch
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_7: Putting an item on it sets it off
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_8: If an inventory is the target, it waits until there is room for the item
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_9: The value panel lets you set a required stack size
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_10: From then on, it only fires once the stack it holds reaches that size
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector.text_11: Players and mobs that step onto an Ejector always set it off
bearing.guide.weighted_ejector_tunnel.te: Put a Brass Tunnel and an Ejector together to split exact amounts off a stack
Set the Brass Tunnel to 'Prefer Nearest' first, so its side exit is used first
How many items peel off is set by the Ejector's stack size
A stack of exactly that size leaves through the side and is thrown away...
...while the rest carries on along the belt
An Ejector that receives a redstone signal will not fire
An Observer facing the Ejector notices every launch
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.header: Building a Grid of Mechanical Crafters
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_1: Lay Mechanical Crafters out in a grid and they will craft any recipe for you
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_2: [Right-Click] them with a Wrench to change the direction of their paths
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_3: Every path must end up at one single exit, which may be on any side
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_4: The result is delivered into whatever storage sits at that exit
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_5: Without rotation, none of the crafters will move
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_6: Items can be placed by hand with a [Right-Click] on a crafter's face
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_7: Crafting kicks off the moment every slot on the paths is filled
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter.text_8: If a recipe leaves some crafters empty, a redstone pulse forces it to start anyway
bearing.guide.mechanical_crafter_connect: Machines can insert items into Crafters on their own
Use a Wrench on the backs of Crafters to merge their inputs together
Now one input point fills every crafter linked to it
A recipe with a gap needs an extra crafter to carry the path across it
A Crafter Slot Cover makes a crafter count as an empty slot in the grid
Covered crafters do not break a shared input made with a Wrench
bearing.guide.deployer.text_1: Feed it rotation and a Deployer acts the way a player's hand would
bearing.guide.deployer.text_2: Its target is always the block two spaces ahead of it
bearing.guide.deployer.text_3: A block right in front of it does not get in the way
bearing.guide.deployer.text_10: Pass it an item by [Right-Clicking] its front
bearing.guide.deployer.text_11: Other machines can keep it stocked as well
bearing.guide.deployer.text_12: There is a filter slot on a Deployer, too
bearing.guide.deployer.text_13: Once filtered, it stays idle unless the item in its hand passes
bearing.guide.deployer.text_14: From then on it accepts only items that pass the filter...
bearing.guide.deployer.text_15: ...and gives up only the ones that fail it
bearing.guide.deployer_modes.text_1: Out of the box, a Deployer performs a [Right-Click]
bearing.guide.deployer_modes.text_2: A Wrench switches it to performing a [Left-Click] instead
bearing.guide.deployer_processing.text_1: Give a Deployer a suitable item and it works on whatever lies underneath
bearing.guide.deployer_processing.text_2: Drop the input onto a Depot under it, or place it there yourself
bearing.guide.deployer_processing.text_4: ...the Deployer holds each one in place, works on it, then lets it go
bearing.guide.deployer_redstone.text_1: While it receives a redstone signal, a Deployer stays idle
bearing.guide.deployer_redstone.text_2: A cycle that has already begun is still finished before it stops
bearing.guide.deployer_redstone.text_3: So a short break in the signal triggers exactly one cycle
bearing.guide.deployer_contraption.text_: When a Deployer is carried along by a moving contraption...
...it acts at every spot it passes, taking items from any inventory on the contraption
Its filter slot chooses which items it pulls from them
Point a Mechanical Saw upward and it becomes a cutting station for many items
The cut item leaves in the direction opposite to the rotation feeding the saw
A saw can sit right in the middle of a belt line
When one input has several possible results, the filter slot picks which one you get
With no filter, the saw takes turns producing each possible result
bearing.guide.mechanical_saw_breaker.tex: Powered, a Mechanical Saw fells any tree standing right in front of it
To bring the whole tree down, the saw must cut the bottom log that holds it to the ground
bearing.guide.mechanical_saw_contraption: A Saw mounted on a moving contraption...
...brings down any tree it is driven against
bearing.guide.mechanical_drill.text_1: Given rotation, a Mechanical Drill mines out the block it faces
bearing.guide.mechanical_drill.text_2: The faster it spins, the faster it mines
bearing.guide.mechanical_drill_contrapti: A Drill mounted on a moving contraption...
...digs out every block it is driven against
